goal: Route each stakeholder's question to the one proved decision that answers it, in that stakeholder's view, so the product shows every reader only what they need.

app.name: stakeholder-view
app.title: Stakeholder view
app.purpose: Decide, as a DMN decision table with hit policy FIRST, which decision app answers a stakeholder's question, from the stakeholder's viewpoint and the kind of question they ask, or that the question is outside their view.
limits: It routes; the app it names gives the answer.
The words each view uses are the product record's, prism/product.json.

fields.name: viewpoint
fields.means: the ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 viewpoint: platform, cloud, operations, security, engineering leadership or business

fields.name: need
fields.means: the question: does the registry conform, is this address admitted, where is my upload, can this storage go, may this image run, can we roll out

meanings.outside-view: this question belongs to another stakeholder's view

rules.why: prism/product.json viewpoint platform (Platform engineering): the registry question is answered by conformance-verdict
prism/product.json viewpoint platform (Platform engineering): the address question is answered by kappa-label-check
prism/product.json viewpoint cloud (Cloud engineering): the upload question is answered by upload-session
prism/product.json viewpoint cloud (Cloud engineering): the image question is answered by vm-image-admission
prism/product.json viewpoint operator (Operations and SRE): the storage question is answered by gc-eviction
prism/product.json viewpoint operator (Operations and SRE): the upload question is answered by upload-session
prism/product.json viewpoint operator (Operations and SRE): the registry question is answered by conformance-verdict
prism/product.json viewpoint security (Security and supply chain): the image question is answered by vm-image-admission
prism/product.json viewpoint security (Security and supply chain): the address question is answered by kappa-label-check
prism/product.json viewpoint leader (Engineering leadership): the rollout question is answered by rollout-gate
prism/product.json viewpoint business (Business and risk): the storage question is answered by gc-eviction
prism/product.json viewpoint business (Business and risk): the rollout question is answered by rollout-gate

app.otherwiseWhy: prism/product.json: each view names only the apps its stakeholder needs

properties.why: an engineering leader is never handed a protocol-level address check
a business owner is never handed a protocol-level address check
the leader's rollout question always reaches the rollout gate
security's image question always reaches image admission

stakeholders.name: Platform engineer
stakeholders.text: Builds the internal platform and its golden paths, and needs one honest verdict that a registry speaks kappa-distribution before teams depend on it.
concerns: Every reader is routed to the decision that answers them

stakeholders.name: Cloud engineer
stakeholders.text: Moves images, VM disks and datasets between clouds and sites, including air-gapped ones, and needs the same image to be admitted the same way everywhere.
concerns: Every reader is routed to the decision that answers them

stakeholders.name: Registry operator
stakeholders.text: Runs the registry day to day and needs storage reclaimed without ever losing content a tag, pin, finalizer or upload still needs.
concerns: Every reader is routed to the decision that answers them

stakeholders.name: Security engineer
stakeholders.text: Owns supply-chain integrity and needs every image the platform runs to be signed, matching and from an allowed source.
concerns: Every reader is routed to the decision that answers them

stakeholders.name: Engineering leader
stakeholders.text: Decides when the platform ships and needs one word, go, hold or no-go, with the reason, not a test report.
concerns: Every reader is routed to the decision that answers them

stakeholders.name: Business owner
stakeholders.text: Pays for storage and answers for data loss, and needs both kept down without reading the protocol.
concerns: Every reader is routed to the decision that answers them

concerns.name: Every reader is routed to the decision that answers them
concerns.text: Each viewpoint and need lands on one proved decision, or is told it is outside that view.

components.name: Prism page
components.text: The published GitHub Pages site: it checks the holo seal, sends the request to the verified guest in the browser and shows the answer in the reader's view.

threats.name: Leader handed a protocol check
threats.text: A leader asking about addresses is routed to the raw kappa-label check and acts on a detail outside their view.

control.name: Proved routing
control.text: Leader and business viewpoints are never routed to kappa-label-check, proved for every request.

quality.text: A leader asking about a rollout always reaches the rollout gate.
quality.measureText: Requests leader rollout answered other than rollout-gate.
